heard: NASA is dropping a titanium beach ball into a 900-degree hellscape. Venus features a surface hot enough to melt lead and crushing pressure 90 times greater than Earth's. In 2021, NASA selected the DAVI-NCI mission to pierce the planet's toxic clouds of sulfuric acid. The heart of the mission is a titanium sphere built to survive a one-hour plunge through the crushing air. This descent probe will sniff noble gases to discover if Earth's twin once held vast water oceans. Before crashing, the sphere will capture the first high-resolution views of Venus's rugged mountains since 1982. Named after Leonardo da Vinci, this is NASA's first atmospheric entry into Venus since the 1970s. It is a daring, high-stakes journey into a 900-degree hellscape.
